findings.body: `queryset[start_offset:stop]` slices a Django QuerySet with a negative start index, which raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`. This is not caught by paginate()'s BadPaginationError handler and surfaces as an unhandled HTTP 500.
findings.evidence: start_offset = cursor.offset  # Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination
findings.failure_mode: Runtime exception escapes as a 500 on the audit-log endpoint.
findings.impact: `queryset[start_offset:stop]` slices a Django QuerySet with a negative start index, which raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`. This is not caught by paginate()'s BadPaginationError handler and surfaces as an unhandled HTTP 500.
findings.root_cause: New negative-offset code path slices a Django QuerySet with a negative start, which the ORM forbids.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not pass negative indices to a Django QuerySet slice; clamp the offset with `max(0, cursor.offset)` (as done in the else branch) or reject negative cursor offsets with a BadPaginationError.
findings.title: Negative queryset offset raises ValueError (HTTP 500)
findings.trigger: A superuser or member with has_global_access calls the audit-log endpoint with `optimized_pagination=true` and a crafted cursor whose offset is negative (e.g. `cursor=1700000000000:-1:0`), so `cursor.offset < 0` and `enable_advanced_features` is True.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 877-882 show when enable_advanced_features=True and cursor.offset<0, start_offset is set to cursor.offset (negative) and queryset[start_offset:stop] is executed. Django QuerySets raise ValueError on negative indexing. The BadPaginationError handler in paginate() won't catch ValueError, causing HTTP 500.
